title: 中央瑞音又响了  (Middle D Sings Again)

segments.t: By Tuesday morning the rain has cleared, and inside Room 9 Chen sets down his tweezers beside the open piano while Teacher Song takes her seat on the wooden bench. Listen first.
宋老师，新的毛毡轴套干了，黄铜轴销也装紧了。
老陈，您的手像钟表匠一样稳。我可以试试这个琴键吗？
请尽管弹——先轻轻按，再用十足的力气。
听……瑞音！清亮、圆润，木头里一点杂音都没有！
跟上面那个音比起来，听着是不是稍微低了一点儿？
老陈，您的耳朵真灵！把钢调音扳手往右拧一丝丝。
就在这儿……到了您就喊停。
就……这儿！稳住！跟我一起弹一个温暖的索大调和弦——听！
瞧瞧——这台老核桃木琴箱把整间玻璃房都装满了！
老陈，等明天下午您听听周经理姑姑那首写完的圆舞曲吧。
我把前面板拧回去，再把黄铜踏板擦亮。
谢谢您，老陈。安静了三十年，这架钢琴终于找回自己的声音了。
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
宋老师，新的毛毡轴套干了，黄铜轴销也装紧了。
'The new felt bushing is dry and the brass pin sits tight, Teacher Song.' Adding 'tight' directly after the verb 'install' tells us the result in two syllables: fitted in and sitting snug.
老陈，您的手像钟表匠一样稳。我可以试试这个琴键吗？
'Your hands are as steady as a watchmaker's, Chen. May I try the key?' A watchmaker is literally a 'clock-watch craftsman', using Mandarin's classic ending for skilled tradespeople.
请尽管弹——先轻轻按，再用十足的力气。
'Go right ahead—gently first, then full weight.' Notice 'ten-sufficient' for 'full': in Chinese, ten parts out of ten means one hundred percent.
听……瑞音！清亮、圆润，木头里一点杂音都没有！
'Listen... D! Clear, round, and zero rattle in the wood!' Unwanted buzz or rattle in an instrument is literally 'mixed sound' in Mandarin, contrasting neatly with pure 'clear-bright' tone.
跟上面那个音比起来，听着是不是稍微低了一点儿？
'Sounds a tiny bit flat next to the note above it, doesn't it?' Where English musicians say a note is 'flat', Mandarin simply says it is 'low' by a tiny bit.
老陈，您的耳朵真灵！把钢调音扳手往右拧一丝丝。
'You have a good ear, Chen! Turn the steel tuning wrench a hair to the right.' Calling someone's ears 'spirited' is the natural Mandarin phrase for a keen musical ear.
就在这儿……到了您就喊停。
'Right here... tell me when to stop.' Literally 'arrived, then you shout stop'—five crisp everyday words with no extra connecting glue needed.
就……这儿！稳住！跟我一起弹一个温暖的索大调和弦——听！
'Right... there! Hold it! Play a warm G-major chord with me—listen!' A musical chord is literally 'harmony-strings', picturing several piano strings ringing together as one.
瞧瞧——这台老核桃木琴箱把整间玻璃房都装满了！
'Look at that—this old walnut box fills the whole glass room!' Chen's warm 'look-look' at the start invites Teacher Song to marvel at the sound filling the room.
老陈，等明天下午您听听周经理姑姑那首写完的圆舞曲吧。
'Wait until you hear Manager Zhou's aunt's finished waltz tomorrow afternoon, Chen.' In Mandarin, a waltz is literally a 'round-dance song', painting the whirling circles right in the name.
我把前面板拧回去，再把黄铜踏板擦亮。
'Let me screw the front panel back on and polish the brass pedals.' Piano pedals are literally 'step-boards', built from the words for stepping with your foot and wooden board.
谢谢您，老陈。安静了三十年，这架钢琴终于找回自己的声音了。
'Thank you, Chen. After thirty quiet years, this piano has its voice back.' Teacher Song uses the respectful 'you' right back with Chen, honouring his patient craftsmanship.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
宋老师，新的毛毡轴套干了，黄铜轴销也装紧了。
老陈，您的手像钟表匠一样稳。我可以试试这个琴键吗？
请尽管弹——先轻轻按，再用十足的力气。
听……瑞音！清亮、圆润，木头里一点杂音都没有！
跟上面那个音比起来，听着是不是稍微低了一点儿？
老陈，您的耳朵真灵！把钢调音扳手往右拧一丝丝。
就在这儿……到了您就喊停。
就……这儿！稳住！跟我一起弹一个温暖的索大调和弦——听！
瞧瞧——这台老核桃木琴箱把整间玻璃房都装满了！
老陈，等明天下午您听听周经理姑姑那首写完的圆舞曲吧。
我把前面板拧回去，再把黄铜踏板擦亮。
谢谢您，老陈。安静了三十年，这架钢琴终于找回自己的声音了。
Middle D rings clear and true, and the walnut upright piano is ready for Wednesday's big afternoon. See you next time.
下次见！
